messages.author: a771569918076f9f
messages.subject: Msstats 3.8.2  and Spectronaut professional 10.0
parts:
Dear all,


I'm currently having some issue using MSstas to analyze data from Spectronaut Professional 10.0. By the way, Im new in using both Spectronaut and MSstats....


Spectronaut: version 10.0 Professional (x64)
MSstats: I'm using directly the source code from MSstats v 3.8.2

Issue1:
- In Spectronaut at the "Report" perspective. I used the "MSstats Fragment Report" option and exported my data. Its a huge dataframe with >2.000.000 rows

- In MSstats, I used the exported data from Spectronaut and ran the "DataProcess.R" code as recommended for DIA experiment from Spectronaut:


step1 <-  dataProcess(mydata,
                      normalization=  'equalizeMedians',
                      featureSubset="all",
                      summaryMethod="TMP",
                      cutoffCensored="minFeature",
                      censoredInt="0",
                      MBimpute=TRUE,
                      maxQuantileforCensored=0.999)



- I got the warning message that my data contains duplicate rows

- But when I exported my data in Spectronaut with the columns required for "SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat.R" code (default settings) and ran its output with "DataProcess.R" (as described above). There was no warning message regarding the duplicate rows anymore.

- I was just wondering what was the difference then between the preformating in Spectronaut and the formating code "SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat.R"



Issue2:

- I used the output from "SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat.R" code as input for "DataProcess.R" (settings as described aboved, I tried both censoredInt="0" & censoredInt="NA" )

- I got the error message 

 == Start the summarization per subplot...
Getting the summarization by Tukey's median polish per subplot for protein  A0AVF1 ( 1  of  6578 )
*** error : can't summarize per subplot with TMP.

- Do you have any ideas why it happened?


Issue3:

- There was no error message regarding the subplot when I ran "DataProcess.R" code with featureSubset="top3"

- But these messages appeared:

 
Error: cannot allocate vector of size 12.3 Gb
 
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In unique(.Internal(unlist(lapply(x, levels), recursive, FALSE))) :
  Reached total allocation of 8073Mb: see help(memory.size)
2: In unique(.Internal(unlist(lapply(x, levels), recursive, FALSE))) :
  Reached total allocation of 8073Mb: see help(memory.size)

- I guessed it reached the limit of memory capacity of my computer (8 GB of RAM, 7.8 GB was avaiable, 64 Bit system). I changed to a computer with 24 GB of Ram. I still have the same issue
- If this is an issue with my analysis, then I curious to know the reason....
- If this is an issue with my computer, then is it possible to not plot the subplot for each of the proteins? I have more then 6000 proteins identified in my data...

If you need further infos from my side, dont hesitate to contact me. And thanks in advance for any ideas

Best regards
Chi

messages.author: df9ba0266a9a081f
messages.subject: Re: Msstats 3.8.2  and Spectronaut professional 10.0
parts:
Dear Chi,

You should use 'SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat' function with Spectronaut output, before using dataProcess function.

Issue 1:
- I was just wondering what was the difference then between the preformating in Spectronaut and the formating code "SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat.R"

---> There are some preprocessing step. Please check p49 in manual.

Issue 2:
-  Do you have any ideas why it happened?

---> I recommend to check profile plot for that protein. It shows how the data look like. I suspect that there are many missing in that protein.

Issue 3: 
- limit of memory
---> Thank you for reporting it. We realized this issue and are updating code. We will update next version as soon as possible.

Hope to help.

- Meena
